review_text:
It's no Peaky Blinders but some might enjoy it
House of Guinness is a new show from Steven Knight (Peaky Blinders). It has that same look and feel as PB. It's about the Guinness family after its founder dies in 1868 and leaves its empire in the hands of his four children, each with problems and secrets of their own. It may start slow for some but stay with it because after the first couple episodes it really picks up. It's a good period series about power, greed, betrayal and back stabbing. Bottom line is while House of Guinness isn't nearly as good as PB, it's still a pretty good show that's worth watching.

Don't compare it to Peaky Blinders
Being a huge fan of Peaky Blinders I was really looking forward to House of Guinness ever since I first heard about it since it has the same creator in Steven Knight. Now, I didn't think it going to be as good as Peaky Blinders bc not much is so don't go into this trying to compare. Knight sure knows how to make a show entertaining while staying true to its history. You're never bored as the show flys by. Just be sure you give yourself enough time to watch this because once you start you're going to want to binge it as quickly as possible.

Good if you're not expecting Peaky Blinders
I was looking forward to this for a few couple months when I saw it was from the creator of Peaky Blinders. It took a couple episodes to get into but once I did, I really enjoyed it. It looks like Peaky Blinders but that's about as far as similarities go and if you're not looking for a Peaky 2.0, you should enjoy it. I agree with other reviews though, the music does not fit it and I hope they change it in season two.

8 from 7.5 and my wishes
I was really curious about the Guinness family ever since I visited the Republic of Ireland and our tour guide told us that they were loved and respected by Irish people. Tbh until that they Guinness was just a beer brand to me which I really love and of course nobody can be loved by 100%. So watching their story with a good cinematography together with some good performers was enjoyable. And I am a sucker for sound of Irish flute, so I hyped whenever I heard it BUT I was really annoyed whenever I heard techno and rap music even though I mainly listen those two. Maybe the idea behind is to get attention from new gens but still it just ruined the atmosphere. My second dislike was the Netflix scenes. You know what I mean. The substance, the intimacy and the community which I really love everyone and everything BUT whenever Netflix includes these topics "nearly all the time" they just feel like ads and loose the meaning😔 Sorry for my English.

Enjoy it but also disappointing
Been looking forward too this show for a while. Watched a couple of episodes today. It's a good story, decent actors & the scenery is excellent. What disappoints me is the modern take of putting modern music in a historical show. Hip hop & up beat tunes have no place in a series set in the 19 century. It completely ruin the feel of the historical time.

Thirsty For Season 2
'House of Guinness' successfully navigates a tricky path. It would have been very easy to cross over from drama to soap opera, but this series does not. I also don't care that they have invented some characters, Sean Rafferty (James Norton), or fudged dates. This is not a documentary.The acting is quite good with Anthony Boyle (Arthur Guinness) being particularly strong. Also, Jack Gleeson (Byron Hedges), Michael McElhatton (Potter), Niamh McCormack (Ellen Cochrane) and Louis Partridge (Edward Guinness).There are some unusual accents, but such is life. I look forward to Season 2.

Irish Peaky Blinders
In the wake of the passing of the head of the Guinness family the offspring - three brothers, one sister - are left to pick up the pieces, whilst being forced to address their own issues & failings amidst the backdrop of an Ireland on the brink of revolution and retribution. Highly stylised and with a modern soundtrack out of kilter with the historic setting this has more than a passing resemblance to Peaky Blinders. Good cast, the ever reliable James Norton and relative newcomer Emily Fairn (wonderful in The Responder) stand out in particular. It looks great and It's enough to hold the attention but feels a bit forced and for me, doesn't quite gel. That said I wasn't a fan of the aforementioned Peaky Blinders and I think that did quite well...!

Elegant production, acting and scenery
You have to read the disclaimer at the start of each episode indicating that this is a 'fictionalized" account of the Guinness history...than enjoy the show.Opulent sets and AI reflect the massive wealth of the family and the street scenes are equally well-done.For entertainment to serve its purpose it should be done correctly as promised, feature a disclaimer if it is not historically accurate and have enough value to make viewers want to see the next chapter in the series. I believe this meets all that criteria but dropped a star rating by using an ill-considered ending to the series.

For Entertainment
I think what the people writing the few reviews that were posted are forgetting is that "House of Guinness" is not an accurate biographical documentary of the Guinness family during the mid-19th century. As said in the beginning of the show it is 'inspired' by their story. "House of Guinness" is a television series for entertainment purposes. And I found it entertaining. I'm sure that the people criticizing the Irish accents in the show are Irish themselves and can distinguish correct accents. Deduct a point for that.

Incredible series
A beautifully filmed series with beautiful costumes and scenery. If the series Peaky Blinders and Succession had a baby but better. The soundtrack is great too with classic songs that get your feet moving. The actors are solid as well and easy on the eyes. A must watch for Irish history buffs and fans of great story telling. Highly recommend.

Interesting..
I really wanted to love this series. However, I decided to look into why the Guiness family barely sounds Irish. Learning that the family was very associated with the English aristocracy and was against the Nationalist movement was disappointing. The show itself isn't too bad. But don't watch this with the expectation that it is a great "Irish" show. I could also do without some of the more modern sounding music. I will watch more of it as it does keep one's attention and is rather entertaining.

Enjoying it so far
It's got good action and pace, the actors give a good performance and I like the scenery and music.Whether it's accurate is irrelevant to me, if I want to watch period drama I'll watch Wolf Hall (excellent). This is dramatic and accessible with modern music and language. If that's not for you, watch something else.The people complaining really do need to lighten up!

Average Show
Lukewarm attempt to be the Irish version of Succession, but it didn't quite get the job done. The series appeared to focus on entertaining the teenage/twenty-something demographic. The soundtrack was mostly modern Irish music that significantly distracted from the 19th Century setting of the series.

It has successfully put me to sleep
First of all, is it just my tv or is the whole series filmed in a green ish hue? Kinda how Mexico is always yellow hue in tv series, what is this green supposed to be irish? Cheap trick in my opinion.Second of all, weak actors, not very convincing, dialogue falls flat, the main actors not gonna lie are not that attractive or intriguing. Same old plot, a drunk brother, a mastermind brother, a prude smart sister, etc etc
It also starts rushed, father in the ground, we never got to meet him at all to get at least a glimpse of his behaviour.Music is terrible, overall it's just so boring and doesn't keep me hooked or rooting for anyone.The creators, producers, casting directors could've done better, my message to them is, you had the resources, the money, the influence, the immense legacy of Peaky Blinders, thousands or however many people in your team and you still fell flat. Did no one out of let's say a hundred people say this isn't it? I mean it's new age netflix too, what can we expect besides some failed soap operas with boujee cinematography.And the men actors in this series, they re just so unconvincing, no one is tough, even the drunkard doesn't seem too sure of his drunkness. Do better!!!

REALLY ENTERTAINING!
I didn't think I'd get far into this but ended up watching the whole thing at once.Sure, it's fictional, the story's woven from "true" accounts but all tv shows are like that unless they're documentaries.The actors are all well cast and bring the characters to life convincingly.The costumes and set construction/dressing are impeccable, down to every detail.It's beautifully filmed and lit, the audio is well mixed, I particularly liked the song mix selection.A thoroughly entertaining show that moves at a good pace and is very watchable.

Best Steven show since peaky blinders
Really fun! Succession storylines between dysfunctional families are always fascinating to watch. Anthony boyle is by far the best thing about the show. Louis partridge impressed me with a range i didn't know he had and his and anthony's brotherly chemistry was great. James norton was aura farming the entire time and i had no qualms about it. Hope it gets renewed for a season 2.

It gets better through time
The 1st episode is atrocious and all over the place, especially with the random choices of modern music (Guardians of the Galaxy vibe), but it gets much better and clearer through time.The best part of the show is for sure the story itself, it is very captivating, and the visual production.On the other hand, it seems way too Netflix-y. The acting is often over the top, some dialogues are very banal and some storylines and characters are oversimplified. As a foreigner living in Ireland, I have a feeling that the Irish characters are shown as presented as caricatures and the accent is so rarely on point, that it's getting very annoying.

Brilliant
Loved it and the showing off of all the Irish music! Kneecap, Fontaines & Lankum! Great to see so many great Irish actors in this too. Really loved Danielle Galligan, Jack Gleason and Ann Skelly. Louis Patridge was so so good. Great that they touched on the famine and the after effects and the role of Guinness in it.

Style over substance
Looks good, feels over the top. Acting ok some good cast. Watched two episodes. Don't feel the need to watch anymore. The soundtrack is super cool, but doesn't connect to the feel. Its definitely no peaky blinders, but does feel like it wants to be. It may have worked to help us connect to the characters if we had perhaps seen the dad in action before his passing.

Nice show
House of Guinness is a surprisingly enjoyable watch. I really liked it - the set design is impressive, with tons of detailed decorations that give the story real atmosphere. On top of that, it's shot beautifully, with great attention to visuals and mood. Even if the plot isn't groundbreaking, the style and production value make it worth seeing.

Diddle iddle set in Dublin
Calling the Guinness family 'Irish' is like calling Prince William 'Welsh' but it is fun to watch !Hilda Fay as 'Sultan' was as close to an actual Irish human as the drama managed, although Michael McElhatton's character was gas too. Less 'Downton' and deferential than an English butler.The producer is English and perhaps that's why he thinks so many Irish people wore 'Green' or was that something for the US audience? The idea that a catholic would go to a protestant ceremony in those days shows a total lack of understanding. Former protestant President Douglas Hyde died in 1949 and the catholic government stayed outside the building, not crossing the threshold.In fairness the soundtrack did include Irish performers but shocking few female voices, like in the script. I hope Ms Kirwan will get to spread her wings next Season. Her talents were woefully under utilised.This show will likely cause more lemmings to visit the 'Storehouse' where they keep pictures on a wall.For those in Delgany or other enclaves, this is likely what former Catholics who crossed the aisle aspire to! Now that we have marriage equality / abortion - you don't have to be CoI to cavort wildly in the Wicklow hills and woods without fear of consequences.

Steampunk chaos meets Bridgerton
Many viewers will find the Peaky Blinders steampunk chaos of the first episode hard to follow. It's meant to be emblematic of the chaos in the characters' lives following the patriarch's death. Once the characters find their grooves, the narrative evolves more gently, becoming more like Sofia Coppola's Marie Antoinette or Bridgerton.Let's be clear: this is not meant to be a historically accurate film, though it is more connected to reality than Bridgerton.The accents are mostly authentic, so please watch with the subtitles on.

A Compelling Look at the Guinness Legacy
House of Guinness is a gripping period drama about the turbulent Guinness brewing dynasty in 19th-century Dublin, focusing on the third generation. Family intrigue, political tension, and personal secrets give each character depth, making the story both compelling and binge-worthy.James Norton plays Sean Rafferty, a fictional character who is complex - at times menacing, at times kind, and sometimes hard to read, though Norton's good looks may make conveying menace difficult.The series portrays Edward Guinness as exporting Guinness to the US (not strictly true, though he did expand and modernize the business) and depicts his philanthropic ideas as inspired by his wife and sister. It therefore positions him to be awarded the Earl of Iveagh (possibly in Season 2). Some accents and period details feel off, but the historical context, layered characters, and engaging drama kept me watching.

Hard to fathom for non-Irish
Amazing dramatisation of the history of the Guinesses. For everyone who is not acquainted with the influence this family had over the modern history of Ireland as we know it - this piece of opulent television series might be able to shed a bit of light on it. Amongst historical inaccuracies it still manages to shine a light on the complex relationship between the necessities of survival under the British rule and the start of the urge to strive for independence based on Irish traits such as hard work and a strong sense of belonging. My only concern is that people who are not familiar with Irish history might find themselves in over their heads.

Four Stars for the Style and Sets
But that's it. Writing so contrived I didn't make it to the end of the first episode. Some of the actors already seeming quite poor (those outside the family) and the modern music just didn't work for me. Trying too hard to be a Peaky Blinders reboot but missing the mark.I'll keep an eye on other reviews and if others rate it, I might try again.

Which generation will stuff it up?
With a long line of familial succession in the Guinness business, Anne, Arthur, Benjamin and Edward, have a lot to live up to. The family division is made clear at the reading of the will, but the division of intellect unfolds requiring all siblings to play a role for the sake of the family name.The personalities of the four children, their right-hand men, their female relatives and their opposition all played vital parts in progressing or hindering the business, and in turn, forcing the children to grow up.The family's situation contrasted with that of the population and the circumstances of their lives, due to undue prejudice and hate. Bridges built were under constant threat of falling down but those who were strong, whilst putting themselves at risk, sometimes prevailed. A frustrating Irish tale told over and over.The closeups were beautifully photographed, the music catchy, the scenery realistic and the city life vibrant and depressing. I really enjoyed each episode.

It is not a documentary, it is a fictional story, and a good one!
Production is great, dialogues a bit over the top sometimes but still very good, acting is unbelievable good with lots of emotional moments being played to perfection. If you expect the accuracy of a documentary you won't get it. If you want quality entertainment, you've come to the right place.If you worry about the soundtrack, don't. They did add bits and pieces of modern music but most of it it is the jolly Irish tune.

A bit flat
I was really looking forward to this as I love a good pint of Guinness and I know the beer is really nothing to do with this story but it is quite boring. The cinematography and atmosphere are like Peaky Blinders but storyline lets it down.The story is all over the place and doesn't make sense. It says it is is based on true stories which I doubt very much as it is so far fetched.A shame and could have been much better, I would say James Norton was excellent though.

Loved best series in years
Loved this series you do episodes in Castletown carton and leixlip castle owned
Arthur guinness family
Like if you know history spend alot time parties in leixlip guinness family helped poor during famine times
They build obelisk etc structures around leixlip guinness family paid them.Glued this seasonEdward so handsome.

Stout Struggles: Ambitious but Flawed Historical Saga
House of Guinness (Season 1?) pours out a heady mix of family feuds, political intrigue, and 19th-century Dublin grit, but it's a brew that doesn't always go down smooth.Steven Knight crafts a "fictional" tale of the Guinness siblings... Anthony Boyle's guarded Arthur, Louis Partridge's driven Edward, Emily Fairn's fierce Anne, and Fionn O'Shea's shaky Benjamin - with a vivid ensemble (James Norton's menacing Rafferty and Niamh McCormack's fiery Ellen stand out).The show shines when it leans into Anne's reformist heart or Edward's bold schemes, with Ep 3's emotional punch hitting hardest. Nicolai Brüel and Joe Saade's visuals paint a moody, lived-in Ireland, and Ilan Eshkeri's score keeps the pulse steady.But the pacing wobbles... early episodes simmer slowly, mid-season sparks (Ep 6-7), then the finale stumbles with soap opera fluff before a gripping, unresolved cliffhanger. Knight's dialogue crackles, yet repetitive family spats and rushed resolutions dilute the payoff.It's a watchable saga with strong performances and historical heft, but the uneven rhythm and dangling threads leave you thirsty for closure.6.5/10: Solid for drama fans, not quite a classic.
